title: Blow-down Debris — Fallen Pine Trunk Tangle (Pinus sylvestris)
era: Contemporary — forest-steppe / pine bor biome (Ukraine/Russia); war-damaged state

sources.pinus_wiki: Pinus sylvestris — Wikipedia: 'mature 25–35 m (exceptionally >45 m), trunk ~1.0 m DBH (range 0.5–1.3 m, exceptionally >1.7 m), orange-brown upper bark'
sources.pinus_jrc: EU JRC Forest Atlas via research brief — Scots pine trunk diameter range 0.5–1.3 m DBH confirmed
sources.bark_conifers: conifers.org + Wikipedia — 'bark TWO-TONE: lower trunk thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates up to ~5 cm thick; upper trunk + branches thin flaking orange-red/copper'
sources.war_damage: Reuters/VOA 'Ukraine's vast forests devastated'; Grist — war-killed trees = 'field of stumps', 'stripped, broken trunks', 'black sticks', charcoal piles; ~5 million acres burned since 2022
sources.research_brief: Ecology + visual character of Ukrainian/Russian regional landscape biomes — ENGENDROS PURGE world plan (2026-06-10)

trunk_dims.note: 0.60 m DBH = a mid-aged mature specimen within the sourced range. Used as the base diameter for taper derivation.

trunk_diameter_fallen.derivation: Scots pine taper estimated at ~1 cm/m (mid-range for European conifers; exact taper table not independently sourced — see needs[]). At 4 m height above ground: diameter ≈ 0.60 − 2×0.01×4 = 0.52 m. More conservatively mid-span of fallen section ≈ 0.34 m. r=0.17 m used for main cylinder.

butt_diameter.derivation: Butt end of fallen section (nearest the stump): diameter ≈ 0.60 m DBH × 0.73 ≈ 0.44 m → r=0.22 m. Taper factor estimated — see needs[].

branch_diameter_primary.note: Primary scaffold branch at trunk junction. Roughly 1/4 to 1/3 of trunk diameter (general dendrology rule of thumb). 0.16/0.34 ≈ 47% — slightly high but exaggerated for game-prop readability. See needs[].

branch_diameter_secondary.note: Secondary branch and terminal twig (~half of primary branch diameter). Design estimate; see needs[].

foliage_clump.note: Bounding box (~0.30 × 0.18 × 0.40 m) of a dead dried-needle cluster on a fallen pine branch. Pinus sylvestris needles in paired tufts (Wikipedia; bark_conifers). No measured cluster size — design estimate; see needs[].

war_damage_feature.note: Charred/scorched strip on the blast-facing side of the trunk, evidenced by 'black sticks' and charcoal-pile descriptions (Reuters/VOA/Grist). The charBlack scorch band (0.08 × 0.28 × 0.80 m) represents this; its exact dimensions are design estimates derived from the trunk radius.

ground_contact.note: Compressed bare-soil exposure strip under a fallen trunk, slightly narrower than the trunk diameter (0.55 × 0.04 × 2.60 m). Width and length derived from trunk_diameter_fallen. Included for visual grounding; no specific source for ground-impression geometry.

bark_scatter.note: Bark fragments (two small bevelBox pieces) scattered on the ground around the fallen trunk. Pinus sylvestris sheds thick scaly plates on impact; war-damage causes additional fragmentation. Dimensions (0.18 × 0.04 × 0.12 m, 0.12 × 0.04 × 0.15 m) are design estimates.

derivation.src: geometric derivation from trunk_dims + bark_conifers + war_damage_feature
derivation.derivation: scorch height ≈ 0.28 m = top-to-near-ground span on the trunk side; breakFace w,h = trunk diameter 0.34 m rounded to 0.32 m; breakFace d = 0.06 m proud cap to read as exposed end grain

design_estimate.note: Catch-all key for dimensions that are proportionally reasonable but lack a directly quantified source (branch diameters, foliage clump size, bark chip size, log-section length). All flagged in needs[].

feature_inventory.main_trunk: Horizontal fallen pine trunk lying along Z, barkPine two-tone; wider butt at −Z (near old stump), narrower snap end at +Z.
feature_inventory.trunk_butt: Thicker cylinder at the butt/stump end of the trunk; same barkPine, slightly greater radius.
feature_inventory.break_face: Pale exposed heartwood at the +Z snap point: woodMid disc, contrasts dark bark.
feature_inventory.scorch_band: War/fire charring strip on one trunk flank (charBlack thin bevelBox embedded in the side).
feature_inventory.branch_1: Primary scaffold branch lying outward to the right (+X side), barkPine.
feature_inventory.branch_2: Secondary branch to the opposite side (−X), barkPine.
feature_inventory.twig_1: Thin terminal twig off the end of branch_1, barkDark.
feature_inventory.foliage_1: Dead dried-needle cluster near branch_1 end, foliageDry rust-orange.
feature_inventory.foliage_2: Dead dried-needle cluster near branch_2 end, foliageDry.
feature_inventory.ground_soil: sandSoil exposure strip where trunk rests — scraped/compressed earth.
feature_inventory.bark_chip_1: Small barkDark bark fragment to the right of the trunk.
feature_inventory.bark_chip_2: Small barkDark bark fragment to the left.

game_model_purpose: World cover prop — a blown-down pine tangle offering low crouch cover. Distinct from log_fallen (single clean log): this is a multi-piece blown-down assemblage with branches, dead foliage, and war-damage scorch — marks blast/fire zones in the forest-steppe or pine bor biome.
needs: Scots pine stem taper rate (cm/m) from a forestry reference — current estimate (~1 cm/m, giving r=0.17 m at mid-span) is unverified; a taper table would confirm or correct trunk_diameter_fallen and butt_diameter
Primary branch diameter at trunk junction for mature Scots pine — a silviculture or wood-anatomy source (current 0.16 m is a rule-of-thumb estimate)
Typical blown-down or artillery-felled trunk section length — current 3.0 m is a design estimate with no field or forestry source
Foliage cluster bounding box for dead Pinus sylvestris needles — no measured cluster size found in sources reviewed
Bark chip dimensions for impact-shed pine bark — not quantified in any source reviewed
